archetypes.name: contract-sync
archetypes.rationale: Plan modifies both .sh scripts and their sibling .md contract docs; gaps between code changes and contract updates would leave wire-format docs stale or inconsistent.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan changes both design-pause-load.sh and design-log-publish.sh AND their respective .md contract siblings. Verify that every behavioral change described for WI2 (new restore mechanism) and WI3 (marker lifecycle inversion) is accurately reflected in the corresponding .md contract updates, including the new WARN=marker-delete-failed output-contract entry and the updated .completed/ allowlist in design-log-publish.md. Check whether the plan's proposed .md wording omits any output key, parameter, or behavior the updated scripts will emit or enforce. Also check whether any existing .md contract text will be left stale — for example, references to git archive in design-pause-load.md or to the old emit_load_fail delete-arg semantics. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: call-site-completeness
archetypes.rationale: WI3 removes the clear_pause_marker delete-arg from every emit_load_fail call site; a missed call site silently preserves the broken behavior with no test catching it.
archetypes.prompt_body: The WI3 fix requires removing the true delete argument from every emit_load_fail call in design-pause-load.sh and stripping the dollar-brace-2-false branch entirely. Read the current design-pause-load.sh and count all emit_load_fail call sites; verify the plan's enumerated list (snapshot-not-found, snapshot-extract-failed, missing-restored-artifact, restored-issue-mismatch, restored-run-id-mismatch, restored-repo-mismatch, invalid-restored-manifest) matches every actual call site in the file. Also check whether the plan's test coverage in test-design-pause-resume.sh covers each distinct failure-path variant so a missed call site would be caught by at least one assertion. If the plan's call-site list is incomplete, identify the missing ones. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: bash-portability
archetypes.rationale: WI2 introduces a NUL-delimited git ls-tree loop; the plan does not explicitly verify Bash 3.2 compatibility for the new read -d NUL pattern per BASH_AUTHORING.md.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan's WI2 replacement uses git ls-tree -r -z --name-only piped into a while IFS= read -r -d '' loop with per-path mkdir -p and git show redirects into a destination file. Verify this pattern is Bash 3.2-safe per the repo's BASH_AUTHORING.md constraints, paying attention to whether the read -d '' NUL-delimiter form and the IFS= read -r quoting pattern behave correctly in Bash 3.2 for paths with spaces or special characters. Also check whether the plan's path-stripping step that replicates --strip-components=3 is precisely specified — a mismatch would silently write artifacts to wrong relative paths inside the restore temp directory. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
